title: Gaps between recordings in the 1970s
summary: Between "Solo Machito" in 1969 and later albums, the band kept working; Machito says he lost exposure to the new generation and never counted his albums.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Okay. Macho, in 1969 you recorded "Solo Machito". You didn't record again until 1972, for Americana, then you didn't record again until 1976. These long absences
of recordings those years apart, does it hurt you, and does it hurt the band.
No, the thing is this. We kept working, not as much as we want to because .....
Is this because of the new recordings?

No, because who has the most exposure. The new generation know more. You just can't fight with the replacement, you just can't fight with exposure, so we - we had our problems. But the people that want to dance, they was dancing with my band, listen to the new one that had all the, I mean, radio exposure and they don't, I mean, expose all those things like second-rate and nothing like that. We was there with all the impact and, as a matter of fact, there wasn't no abuse like, you know, a guy that is punch-drunk or his reflex that's no good. His reflex was there.
I know you got over 200/ RPMs, way over 200. About how many albums would you say you got recorded?
Gee, I never keep track, really.
